prompt.context: Your client is Canyon Capital Partners (CCP). CCP is a long-established hedge fund headquartered in Hartford, CT. Hedge funds make money mainly out of management fees and carried interests. Over the past two years, CCP's profits have been declining.
prompt.question: Its CEO and founder has hired you to help her understand why profits are trending down and what she should do to restore the firm to a more profitable route.

clarifying_info.a: Manage their investors' money to generate above-market investment returns. CCP only invests in US public equity markets.

clarifying_info.q: How much money does CCP manage?
clarifying_info.a: Current assets under management (AuM) are $2.1 billion. In the past three years, the fund has not had any new inflows or outflows of investor money.
Fixed fees paid on the average balance of assets under management. CCP's management fees were 2.0% per year, but were reduced to 1.5% since 2016 because of competitive pressure.
Share of investment performance appropriated by the fund's managers as additional compensation. CCP takes 20% of all investment gains in excess of the 15% hurdle rate in the year.

exhibits.title: AuM & Investment Performance
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart showing Assets under Management (AuM in $mm, left axis) and Investment Performance percentage (right axis) across 2015, 2016, and 2017.
exhibits.data: AuM bars growing from roughly $1,500mm to $2,000mm+; investment performance line at ~20% in 2015, ~5% in 2016, ~0% in 2017.

exhibits.title: Employee Headcount
exhibits.shows: A table of employee headcount by role (C-Suite, Portfolio Managers, Associates, Analysts, Traders, Support Staff) for 2015, 2016, and 2017.
exhibits.data: C-Suite: 3/3/3; Portfolio Managers: 3/3/4; Associates: 7/10/16; Analysts: 13/11/9; Traders: 3/3/3; Support Staff: 7/8/9.

framework: Revenues: analyze trends in the two revenue streams — Management Fees (driven by AuM and fee rate) and Carried Interests (driven by investment performance vs. hurdle rate)
Costs: analyze trends in the major cost buckets — Employee Compensation (headcount and salary mix), Office Rent, Research Materials
External factors (Regulation, Competition, Market Trends) are noted but the primary analysis should focus on internal revenue and cost drivers

questions.prompt: Walk through Exhibit 1. Calculate total revenues for 2015, 2016, and 2017 and identify what is driving the revenue decline.
questions.guidance: Strong answer notices: (1) AuM is steadily increasing, so fee revenue should rise absent rate changes; (2) management fee rate dropped from 2.0% to 1.5% in 2016 causing a fee revenue decrease despite higher AuM; (3) investment performance collapsed from 20% to 5% to 0%, eliminating carried interest revenues entirely after 2015. Candidate should proactively compute each line.

math.setup: Management Fee Revenue = Average AuM x Management Fee %; Carried Interest = (Investment Return - Hurdle Amount) x 20%, where Hurdle Amount = Initial AuM x 15%.
steps: 2015 Carried Interest: Initial AuM=$1,500mm; Total Return=20% => $300mm; Excess Return=$300mm - $1,500mm x 15% = $300mm - $225mm = $75mm; Carried Interest = $75mm x 20% = $15.0mm
2016 Carried Interest: 5% return does not exceed 15% hurdle => $0mm
math.answer: Total revenues fell from $47.0mm in 2015 to $27.0mm in 2016 (-43%) and $28.5mm in 2017. The decline was caused by: (1) management fee rate cut from 2.0% to 1.5% reducing fee revenue despite growing AuM, and (2) investment performance dropping below the 15% hurdle, eliminating all carried interest revenues.

questions.prompt: Walk through Exhibit 2. Calculate total salary costs for 2015, 2016, and 2017 and identify the driver of cost increases.
questions.guidance: Strong answer notices: (1) Associates headcount nearly doubled from 7 to 16 while Analysts shrank from 13 to 9 — Associates earn $250k vs Analysts at $100k, so the mix shift is expensive; (2) total salary increased from $10.175mm to $12.675mm over two years; (3) variable compensation for C-Suite and PMs is tied to fund profitability and is irrelevant to the analysis; (4) office rent and research materials are stable/irrelevant.

math.setup: Total Salary = sum of (headcount x annual salary) for each role. Salaries: C-Suite $1,500,000; Portfolio Managers $500,000; Associates $250,000; Analysts $100,000; Traders $200,000; Support Staff $75,000.
steps: 2015: C-Suite 3x$1.5mm=$4.5mm; PM 3x$0.5mm=$1.5mm; Associates 7x$0.25mm=$1.75mm; Analysts 13x$0.1mm=$1.3mm; Traders 3x$0.2mm=$0.6mm; Support 7x$0.075mm=$0.525mm; Total=$10.175mm
2016: C-Suite $4.5mm; PM $1.5mm; Associates 10x$0.25mm=$2.5mm; Analysts 11x$0.1mm=$1.1mm; Traders $0.6mm; Support 8x$0.075mm=$0.6mm; Total=$10.800mm
2017: C-Suite $4.5mm; PM 4x$0.5mm=$2.0mm; Associates 16x$0.25mm=$4.0mm; Analysts 9x$0.1mm=$0.9mm; Traders $0.6mm; Support 9x$0.075mm=$0.675mm; Total=$12.675mm
math.answer: Total salary costs rose from $10.175mm (2015) to $10.800mm (2016) to $12.675mm (2017). The primary driver is the disproportionate growth in Associates (7→16, cost $1.75mm→$4.0mm) while the cheaper Analyst headcount declined (13→9). This associate-heavy mix shift significantly inflated the cost base.

questions.prompt: Synthesize revenue and cost findings: what is the combined profitability picture?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare total revenues vs. total salary costs and highlight the profit squeeze. Revenues dropped ~40% while costs rose ~25%, compressing margins severely. In 2015 the salary cost ratio was ~22% of revenue; by 2017 it had risen to ~44%.

math.setup: Profit margin proxy = (Total Revenues - Total Salary Costs) / Total Revenues
math.answer: Combined effect: revenues fell 43% from 2015 to 2016 while costs rose, cutting gross profit by more than half and compressing margins from ~78% to ~56%.

recommendation: Increase revenues: raise management fee rate back toward 2.0% if competitive dynamics allow; grow AuM through a new fundraising round; adopt new investment strategies to recover above-hurdle returns and reactivate carried interest income

Reduce costs: restore a healthier analyst-to-associate ratio by promoting meritocracy, reducing associate headcount, and hiring more analysts; implement performance-based promotion criteria to control future mix drift
risks: Increasing management fees may deter existing investors or make fundraising harder in a competitive market
Reducing associate headcount could hurt employee morale and damage CCP's reputation for talent development; cutting staff may also impair future growth capacity
next_steps: Develop a strategy and roadmap for a new fundraising round to grow AuM
Define rules for associate-to-analyst promotion and identify which associates to let go or not renew
Review investment strategy and hiring of investment professionals to improve performance above the 15% hurdle rate
